questions.question: Independence Day is celebrated every year in Pakistan on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14 August**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **14 August** is celebrated as **Independence Day** every year in **Pakistan**.
 
• Independence Day commemorates the day when Pakistan gained **independence from British rule in 1947**.
 
• It is a national holiday in Pakistan, marked by flag-raising ceremonies, parades, cultural events, and patriotic displays.
 
• On this day, the national flag is hoisted on public and private buildings, and special prayers are offered for the prosperity and development of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pakistan was created as a result of the **Pakistan Movement led by the All-India Muslim League** under the leadership of **Muhammad Ali Jinnah**.
 
• The movement sought a separate nation for Muslims in the north-western and eastern zones of British India.
 
• The partition of India and Pakistan led to mass migrations and significant upheaval, impacting millions of lives.
 
• Independence Day is observed with great zeal and enthusiasm across Pakistan, highlighting the country's cultural heritage and national pride.
 
• In **Islamabad, the capital city**, the main celebrations are held at the Presidential and Parliament buildings, where the President and Prime Minister deliver speeches.

questions.question: When is National Handloom Day celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7th August**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Handloom Day **is celebrated on the **7th of August every year**.
 
• The **National Handloom Day was first celebrated in 2015 on the 7th of August** to commemorate the **Swadeshi Movement which was started on this date in 1905**.
 
• This day is celebrated as Handloom day because **Swadeshi Movement encouraged the indigenous industries and in particular handloom weavers**.
 
• It was first inaugurated by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 7th August 2015 in Chennai**.
 
• It comes under the **Ministry of Textiles of the Government of India** headed by **Smriti Irani**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swadeshi Movement** was** launched with the objective of opposing the Bengal Partition**.
 
• It was officially** launched on the 7th of August 1905 at Calcutta Townhall, Bengal**.
 
• The movement promoted the usage of **made-in-India goods and boycotted British-made goods**.
 
• India's one of the most important **Make In India Campaign is based on this Swadeshi Movement**.

questions.question: In India, the National Sports Day is celebrated on which date?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**29th August**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **29th August** is celebrated as the National Sports Day in India.
 
• The day marks the birth anniversary of **Major Dhyan Chand**, one of the greatest hockey players in the history of the sport.
 
• Major Dhyan Chand's achievements in hockey earned India great international recognition, and he is often referred to as the "Wizard of Hockey".
 
• The National Sports Day is celebrated to honor his legacy and to promote sports and physical fitness across the country.
 
• On this day, various events and activities are organized nationwide, including sports competitions, award ceremonies, and fitness drives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Dhyan Chand** was born on 29th August 1905 in Allahabad, India.
 
• He was part of the Indian hockey team that won gold medals in the Olympics in 1928, 1932, and 1936.
 
• In 1956, he was awarded the **Padma Bhushan**, India's third-highest civilian honor, for his contributions to sports.
 
• The National Sports Awards, including the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award, and Dronacharya Award**, are presented by the President of India on this day.
 
• The day aims to raise awareness about the importance of sports and physical activities in leading a healthy and active lifestyle.

questions.question: Statistics Day of India is celebrated each year on 29 June to mark the birth anniversary of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__PC Mahalanobis.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

Key Points__**

__
 
• India celebrates June 29th as the National Statistics Day to recognize the contribution of statistics in daily life and to educate the general public on the importance of statistics in socio-economic planning and policy formulation. The first National Statistics Day was celebrated on 29th June 2007.
 
• The theme of 2020 National Statistics Day is “SDG- 3 (Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages) & SDG- 5 (Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls)”.
 
• June 29th is chosen to celebrate National Statistics Day to commemorate the birth anniversary of Prof. Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, who established the National Statistical System, founder of the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), and contributed to the field of economic planning and statistical development of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• About Prof. Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis :

 
 
• He was known as the “Father of Indian Statistics”.
 
• He was born on 29th June 1893.
 
• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1968 for his contribution to science and services.

questions.question: The Third Battle of Panipat took place in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1761.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Third Battle of Panipat took place on January 14, 1761, between the Marathas and the Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Durrani.
 
• The battle was fought near the city of Panipat, which is now in the Indian state of Haryana.
 
• The Marathas were led by Sadashivrao Bhau, who was supported by other prominent leaders like Vishwasrao, the son of Peshwa Baji Rao I, and Ibrahim Khan Gardi.
 
• **The Afghan forces were led by Ahmad Shah Durrani, who had a well-trained and well-equipped army of around 100,000 soldiers.**
 
• The Third Battle of Panipat was one of the largest and bloodiest battles fought in the 18th century, and it resulted in a decisive victory for the Afghan forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The year 1757 is significant in Indian history as it marks the Battle of Plassey, which was fought between the East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal.**

questions.question: ________ is mainly celebrated by Maharashtrians as New Year's Day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gudi Padwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gudi Padwa:**

 
 
• Gudi Padwa is the Marathi New Year, celebrated primarily in Maharashtra and by Konkani Hindus.
 
• It falls on the first day of the Chaitra month, according to the Hindu lunisolar calendar, typically in March or April.
 
• The festival marks the beginning of the new year and the arrival of spring.
 
• A "Gudi" (a decorated bamboo stick) is raised outside homes, symbolizing victory and prosperity.
 
• It is a time for festive meals, colorful decorations, and celebrating new beginnings.
 
• It is considered an extremely auspicious time, for new ventures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ugadi:**

 
 
• Ugadi is the New Year's Day for the people of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
 
• It also falls on the first day of the Chaitra month.
 
• Like Gudi Padwa, it signifies the start of a new lunar year.
 
• It is celebrated with colorful decorations, special dishes, and religious observances.
 
• The creation of a special pachadi, which is a dish that contains all six tastes, is a very important part of the celebration.
 
 
 
• **Pongal:**
 
 
• Pongal is a harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It typically occurs in mid-January.
 
• It is a four-day festival dedicated to thanking the Sun God for a bountiful harvest.
 
• The festival involves preparing a dish called "Pongal" (sweet rice), decorating homes, and honoring cattle.
 
• The festival marks the end of winter, and the beginning of the suns northward journey.
 
 
 
• **Bihu:**
 
 
• Bihu is a set of three important Assamese festivals in the Indian state of Assam.
 
• Rongali Bihu, also called Bohag Bihu, is the Assamese New Year, celebrated in mid-April.
 
• It marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year and the spring season.
 
• The festival involves traditional dances, music, and feasting.
 
• It is a very colorful festival that brings the entire community together.

questions.question: When is the National Unity Day celebrated in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fri Oct 31 2025 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Unity Day, also known as **Rashtriya Ekta Diwas**, is celebrated in India on **October 31** every year.
 
• This day commemorates the birth anniversary of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, who played a key role in the unification of India.
 
• It was introduced by the Government of India in **2014** to honor Sardar Patel's contributions to national integration.
 
• Various events such as the **"Run for Unity"** are organized across the country to mark this occasion.
 
• The day emphasizes the importance of maintaining the country's unity and integrity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**

 
 
• Also known as the **"Iron Man of India"**.
 
• First Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.
 
• Played a crucial role in the integration of over 500 princely states into the Indian Union.
 
• His efforts and strategies were pivotal in maintaining the nation's unity post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Statue of Unity**
 
 
• Located in the state of Gujarat, India.
 
• It is the world's tallest statue, standing at a height of 182 meters (597 feet).
 
• Dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and inaugurated on October 31, 2018.
 
• Symbolizes Patel's vision of a united India.
 
 
 
• **Run for Unity**
 
 
• An annual event organized on National Unity Day.
 
• Aims to promote national integration and communal harmony.
 
• Participants from various walks of life join to reinforce the message of unity.
 
 
 
• **National Unity Day Pledge**
 
 
• People take a pledge to preserve the unity, integrity, and security of the nation.
 
• Emphasizes the importance of working towards a stronger and more unified India.
 
• Often recited in schools, colleges, and government offices on this day.
